raw.quick_summary: Python bytes is an immutable sequence of integer values from 0 through 255. The values represent raw bytes, not text, so interpreting them as text requires selecting an encoding.

key_concepts.explanation: An immutable sequence whose elements are integer byte values.
An individual integer in the range 0 through 255 that identifies one byte value.
A rule used to interpret byte values as text characters.
A bytes sequence does not specify a text encoding by itself, so its values should not automatically be treated as text.
The act of interpreting bytes as text after choosing an encoding.

concept_map.reason: The central distinction is conceptual: immutable byte values are raw data, while text requires an encoding-based interpretation.

learning_path.title: From Byte Values to Interpreted Text
learning_path.reason: The lesson supports a short conceptual progression from the structure of bytes, through their numeric limits and raw-data status, to encoding-based decoding.

steps.title: Identify Python bytes
steps.learning_goal: Recognize bytes as an immutable sequence of integer values.
steps.explanation: A Python bytes object is a sequence that cannot be changed after creation, and each element is an integer byte value.
steps.connection_to_previous: This is the starting definition for the entire distinction.

steps.title: Understand individual byte values
steps.learning_goal: Distinguish one byte value from the sequence that contains it.
steps.explanation: Each individual element is an integer from 0 through 255. This numeric value identifies a byte, but it is not automatically a character.
steps.connection_to_previous: Once bytes are identified as a sequence, inspect what each element in that sequence represents.

steps.title: Separate raw bytes from text
steps.learning_goal: Understand that bytes do not carry a text encoding by themselves.
steps.explanation: The bytes sequence represents raw byte data. The sequence alone does not say which text encoding, if any, should be used to interpret those values.
steps.connection_to_previous: The numeric nature of byte values explains why they should not automatically be treated as text.

steps.title: Decode using a chosen encoding
steps.learning_goal: Explain why decoding requires an encoding choice.
steps.explanation: To obtain interpreted text, decoding applies a selected text encoding to the byte values. Different encoding choices can affect how the same bytes are interpreted.
steps.connection_to_previous: After distinguishing raw bytes from text, the next idea is the rule needed to connect them: an encoding used during decoding.

checkpoint_questions.question: Which statement best describes a Python bytes object?

options.text: A mutable sequence of text characters.
An immutable sequence of integers representing byte values.
A sequence that always uses UTF-8.
A single integer outside the range 0 through 255.

checkpoint_questions.explanation: Python bytes is an immutable sequence, and its elements are integer byte values.

checkpoint_questions.question: What does an individual integer in a bytes sequence represent?

options.text: One byte value in the range 0 through 255.
The length of the bytes object.

checkpoint_questions.explanation: Each integer identifies one byte value, and valid byte values range from 0 through 255.

checkpoint_questions.question: Why must an encoding be chosen when decoding bytes as text?

options.text: Because each byte sequence automatically contains several encodings.
Because raw bytes do not specify how their values should be interpreted as text.
Because integers cannot have values from 0 through 255.

checkpoint_questions.explanation: A bytes sequence contains byte values but does not itself specify the text encoding needed for interpretation.
